title: Chichinga Suya Goat Kebabs
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: Goat rather than beef, with a wet rub of a hundred and twenty-five grams of ground roasted peanuts — turned every two minutes for medium-rare.
longDesc: The goat version, and the only documented chichinga that uses a wet rub rather than a dry powder: a hundred and twenty-five grams of roasted peanuts ground with three garlic cloves, five centimetres of ginger, cayenne or chilli flakes, smoked paprika and two tablespoons of oil. Four hundred and fifty grams of diced boneless leg of kid goat marinates one to two hours minimum, preferably overnight. The grilling instruction is the most precise of the three: turn every two minutes for medium-rare, or every three for well done, then rest two minutes.
ingredients: 450 g boneless leg of kid goat, diced
A few sprigs of fresh coriander
1 tsp cayenne pepper, or red chilli flakes
Sea salt and coarse black pepper, to taste
steps: Grind the roasted peanuts with the garlic, ginger, cayenne, smoked paprika and 2 tablespoons of oil to a thick rub.
Season with sea salt and coarse black pepper.
Coat the diced goat in the rub.
Marinate 1 to 2 hours minimum, preferably overnight.
Thread onto skewers with the onion and peppers.
Grill, turning every 2 minutes for medium-rare, or every 3 minutes for well done.
Scatter with fresh coriander and serve.
chefTips: Turn every two minutes for medium-rare, every three for well done. That is the most precise grilling instruction in the chichinga record and it works because a wet peanut rub needs constant movement to keep from burning.
A wet rub, not a dry powder — this is what distinguishes this version. Ground roasted peanuts with oil cling differently and char differently from tankora.
Overnight is better than the one-to-two-hour minimum, by her own framing. Goat benefits from the longer marinade.
Rest two minutes after grilling. Short, but it matters on small pieces of goat.
Kid goat, boneless leg, diced. Goat is the more common street meat in Ghana than the sirloin or beef the other documented versions use.
Smoked paprika is her addition and is not traditional. It reinforces the charcoal note if you are grilling indoors.
The seasoning quantities are genuinely ambiguous in the source — both 'to taste' and a specific pinch-and-teaspoon are printed and it is unclear which belongs where. Season by taste.
commonMistakes: Leaving the skewers to sit between turns.
Using a dry powder rub, which belongs to the other versions.
Grinding the peanuts without the oil, which gives a powder rather than a rub.
sources: Adapted from 'Chichinga: Suya Goat Kebabs' by Zoe Adjonyoh, from Zoe's Ghana Kitchen, published on jamieoliver.com. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS). Yield as printed: serves 4; prep 25 minutes plus marinating.

Ingredients exactly as printed. Kebabs: 450g higher-welfare boneless leg of kid goat, diced; 1 large red onion; 1-2 red, green or yellow peppers; groundnut or vegetable oil; a few sprigs of fresh coriander. Spice rub: 125g roasted peanuts; 3 cloves of garlic; 5cm piece of ginger; 1 teaspoon cayenne pepper or red chilli flakes; 1 teaspoon smoked paprika; 2 tablespoons groundnut or vegetable oil.

AN AMBIGUITY IN THE SEASONING, flagged and NOT resolved: one fetch returned 'Sea salt and coarse black pepper to taste' and the other returned '1 pinch sea salt and 1 teaspoon coarse black pepper'. BOTH FORMS ARE PRINTED ON THE PAGE and it could not be determined which belongs to the rub and which to the finished kebabs. The ingredient list above carries the 'to taste' form and the discrepancy is recorded.
Method as printed: marinate 1-2 hours (minimum, preferably overnight); grill 'turn every 2 minutes for medium-rare or every 3 minutes for well done'; rest 2 minutes.
THE TURNING INSTRUCTION is the most precise cooking guidance of the three documented chichinga and is reproduced as a step rather than a tip.
NO SENSORY DONENESS CUE beyond the turning intervals and the medium-rare/well-done distinction.

THE WET RUB is what sets this version apart: 125 g of ground roasted peanuts with oil, against the dry tankora of ground kulikuli and toasted corn flour (GHA061) and the dry two-blend suya system (GHA062). Three named cooks, three different approaches to the same kebab.

THE MEAT also differs across all three: kid goat here, sirloin at GHA062, top round or London broil beef at GHA061, with a chicken variant also published there. No source states a canonical meat for chichinga.
SMOKED PAPRIKA is this author's addition and appears in no other documented chichinga. Flagged rather than removed.
For the full three-way comparison see the sources at GHA061.
storage: Best at once. 2 days refrigerated cooked.
healthBenefits: Goat is leaner than beef or lamb and high in iron and vitamin B12.
Roasted peanuts supply monounsaturated fat, niacin and vitamin E.
Peppers are very high in vitamin C.
culturalNote: Goat is the street meat of West Africa and a wet peanut rub is closer to the Nigerian tsire suya tradition than to the dry tankora dusting of Ghanaian chichinga — which, given this author's Ghanaian-Irish background and London kitchen, is exactly the kind of crossing you would expect. All three documented versions are honestly chichinga.
